record.paper_title: Open problems in PDE models for knowledge-based animal movement via nonlocal perception and cognitive mapping
record.context_brief: Alternative boundary conditions for mark-based model
record.original_question: For the mark-based system ∂_t u_i = d_iΔu_i − γ_i∇·(u_i∇p_i g,R), ∂_t p_i = Σ_j=1^n α_ij u_j − μp_i, in what sense do solutions exist on a bounded domain with a top-hat detection function when the boundary conditions are zero-flux, homogeneous Neumann, or homogeneous Dirichlet rather than periodic?

evidence.quote: Open Problem 9. In what sense do solutions exist solving problem (2.11) subject to zero-flux, homogeneous Neumann, or homogeneous Dirichlet boundary conditions with a top-hat detection function in a bounded domain?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Consider the following nonlocal "mark-based" reaction–advection–diffusion system for n interacting populations on a bounded domain Ω ⊂ R^d (d ≥ 1) with smooth boundary ∂Ω. For i = 1,…,n let u_i(x,t) ≥ 0 denote the density of population i and p_i(x,t) ≥ 0 the density of a chemical/territorial mark associated with population i. The system reads

  ∂_t u_i = d_i Δ u_i − γ_i ∇·( u_i ∇ p_i^{g,R} ),    x ∈ Ω, t > 0,
  ∂_t p_i = Σ_{j=1}^n α_{ij} u_j − μ p_i,    x ∈ Ω, t > 0,

where d_i > 0, γ_i ∈ R, μ > 0 and α_{ij} ∈ R are constants, and the nonlocal perception field p_i^{g,R} is obtained from p_i by convolution with a "top-hat" detection kernel of radius R > 0,

  p_i^{g,R}(x,t) = (g_R * p_i)(x,t),   g_R(y) = (1/|B_R(0)|) 1_{B_R(0)}(y),

with a fixed convention extending p_i outside Ω (e.g. by zero, by reflection, or by restriction of the convolution to Ω ∩ B_R(x)) consistent with the chosen boundary condition. Initial data u_i(·,0) = u_{i,0} ∈ L^∞(Ω), p_i(·,0) = p_{i,0} ∈ L^∞(Ω) are prescribed and non-negative.

Question. In what function-space framework (e.g. weak, mild, strong, classical) and under what conditions on the data do solutions exist (locally or globally in time), and are they unique, when the system is supplemented with one of the following sets of boundary conditions on ∂Ω (in place of periodic boundary conditions):

 (a) zero-flux: ( d_i ∇ u_i − γ_i u_i ∇ p_i^{g,R} ) · ν = 0 on ∂Ω;
 (b) homogeneous Neumann: ∇ u_i · ν = 0 on ∂Ω;
 (c) homogeneous Dirichlet: u_i = 0 on ∂Ω;

where ν is the outward unit normal? Establish existence (and uniqueness/regularity where possible) of solutions in each of these three cases, accounting for the discontinuity of the top-hat kernel g_R.
artifact.status_search_result: Recent work has established existence and uniqueness of global weak solutions for a closely related nonlocal advection–diffusion model with top-hat detection kernel in one spatial dimension, exploiting an embedding property of the top-hat kernel. However, the bounded-domain case in higher dimensions with zero-flux, homogeneous Neumann, or homogeneous Dirichlet boundary conditions (rather than periodic) does not appear to be fully resolved, so the problem appears partially solved.

status_evidence.title: Biological modeling with nonlocal advection–diffusion
status_evidence.snippet: existence and uniqueness of a global weak solution in one spatial dimension using an iterative approach, including potentially discontinuous detection kernels with explicit emphasis on the 'top-hat' detection function
status_evidence.claim: Existence/uniqueness of weak solutions is established in 1D for top-hat kernel models, but multi-D bounded-domain cases with non-periodic BCs are not fully covered.

status_evidence.title: Biological aggregations from spatial memory and nonlocal advection
status_evidence.snippet: nonlocal reaction–diffusion–advection model investigating populations integrating spatial memory and nonlocal detection
status_evidence.claim: Related models have been analyzed but predominantly in 1D or periodic settings.
